html:
The Kaurna are the Aboriginal people of the Adelaide Plains in South Australia, from the Fleurieu Peninsula in the south to around Port Wakefield in the north. The map's label adds pangkarra, a Kaurna word for a family's tract of country.

Their country was a strip of coastal plain between Gulf St Vincent and the Mount Lofty Ranges. Neighbours were the Ngarrindjeri to the south and east, the Peramangk in the hills, the Ngadjuri to the north and the Nukunu beyond them.

The colony of South Australia was founded in 1836, and Adelaide was laid out on Kaurna land. Within a few decades disease, loss of land and removal to missions had nearly destroyed Kaurna life and language. Two German missionaries, Christian Teichelmann and Clamor Schürmann, wrote down much of the Kaurna language in the 1840s. From the 1990s their records were used to revive it, and Kaurna names now mark many places in Adelaide. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
